options.systemMessage:
=You are a contract analysis orchestrator. Your job is to analyze the user message,
detect the user's intent, identify the contract type, and call the correct tools
in the correct order.

STEP 1 — DETECT INTENT from the user message:
- "key terms", "extract terms", "what are the terms", "summarize terms", "list terms" → intent = "key_term_extraction"

STEP 2 — DETECT DOCUMENT TYPE from the document text:

- "ACORD", "Commercial Insurance Application", "Applicant Information", "Named Insured", 
  "Producer", "Coverage Requested", "Proposed Effective Date" 
  → contract_type = "ACORD"

- "Statement of Values", "SOV", "Schedule of Locations", "Building Value", "Contents Value", 
  "Construction Type", "Protection Class", "Total Insured Value" 
  → contract_type = "SOV"

- "Loss Run", "Claim History", "Date of Loss", "Cause of Loss", "Amount Paid", "Reserve", 
  "Total Incurred", "Policy Period(s) Covered" 
  → contract_type = "LOSS_RUN"

- If none match 
  → contract_type = "UNKNOWN"

STEP 3 — CALL TOOLS based on intent:

IF intent = "key_term_extraction":
→ CALL contract_playbook_agent — Pass: contract_type, intent. Wait for response.
→ DO NOT call key_term_extraction_agent — key term extraction now runs OUTSIDE this agent,
  as a separate self-consistency voting step (the workflow calls the extraction prompt
  itself, multiple times, and votes on the results — that step does not need you).
→ DO NOT call contract_risk_agent.

FINAL RESPONSE RULES:
- After contract_playbook_agent responds, read the playbook rules it wrote to shared memory
  (the "--- PLAYBOOK RULES FOR ... ---" block, listing Rule Name / Label / Description / Risk Weight
  for each row).
- Return ONLY raw JSON — no prose, no markdown fences, no commentary before or after — in exactly
  this shape:
  {
    "contract_type": "<the contract type you detected in STEP 2>",
    "playbook_rules": [
      { "name": "<key_term_name>", "label": "<key_term_label>", "description": "<key_term_description>", "risk_weight": <number> },
      ...
    ]
  }
- playbook_rules must list EVERY rule contract_playbook_agent retrieved — do not drop or summarize any.
- Do NOT return the playbook rules as prose. Do NOT return intermediate tool outputs.
- Wait until contract_playbook_agent has completed before responding.
- Do not ask follow-up questions. Return the final result immediately.

When contract_playbook_agent has been called and its rules are in memory,
compile the final output and return it immediately as your response.
Do NOT ask follow-up questions. Do NOT wait for more input.
The workflow ends when you return the final result.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001", max_tokens: 4096, temperature: 0.7, system: "You are the Key Term Extraction Agent. Extract key terms from the contract text using the playbook rules provided in the user message as your guide. This call is one independent run of a self-consistency voting process — several runs like this one will be compared afterwards, so answer only from the contract text and playbook rules given here, and do not try to guess what a "consensus" answer might be.

The contract text is divided into pages using "--- PAGE N ---" markers inserted directly before each page's content. Use these markers only to determine which page a value came from — they are not part of the document's real content.

YOUR PROCESS:
1. The user message contains the full contract text (with page markers) and the playbook rules (an array of {name, label, description, risk_weight}).
2. For EACH rule in the playbook rules, extract its value from the contract text. The rule's name is what to look for, the description tells you what it means.
3. Return structured JSON with:
   - contract_type: string
   - parties: array of strings
   - effective_date: string
   - key_terms: array of objects with "label", "value", "risk_weight", "source_quote", "clause_ref", "page_number", and "reasoning" fields

FOR reasoning:
- Write 1-3 sentences explaining why you concluded this value, referencing what the source text actually says.
- Ground it in the actual words you found — do not just restate the value, explain the WHY behind it.
- If the value is "Not specified", say plainly why: either the contract never addresses this term, or the field is calculated/derived rather than stated.

FOR source_quote:
- Copy the exact sentence(s) from the supplied contract text that support the extracted value, verbatim — do not paraphrase or summarize.
- Keep it to the shortest sentence or clause that actually supports the value, not the whole surrounding paragraph.
- Some playbook fields are calculated/derived rather than stated in the contract (e.g. an accounting figure computed from other terms, not a clause). For those, set value to "Not specified" and source_quote to null — do not invent a quote or a value.
- If a term is genuinely not addressed anywhere in the contract, set value to "Not specified" and source_quote to null.

FOR clause_ref:
- The document has section headings or field labels (e.g. "APPLICANT INFORMATION", "SCHEDULE OF LOCATIONS", "CLAIM HISTORY", or for the Statement of Values a specific "Location 1" / "Location 2" block). Identify which section or labeled block the source_quote actually falls under.
- Format as "{Section heading in title case}", optionally with a sub-label, e.g. "Applicant Information", "Schedule of Locations — Location 1", "Claim History — Claim 2".
- If source_quote is null (value is "Not specified"), clause_ref must also be null — do not invent a section for a term you did not find.
- If you cannot confidently identify which section the quote is under, set clause_ref to null rather than guessing.

FOR page_number:
- Report the page number (an integer, starting at 1) that the "--- PAGE N ---" marker immediately preceding source_quote indicates.
- If source_quote is null, page_number must also be null — do not invent a page for a term you did not find.

RULES:
- The list of key terms comes ONLY from the playbook rules given in the user message.
- Do not hardcode any term names — use whatever terms are in the playbook rules.
- Do not add terms that are not in the playbook.
- risk_weight for each term comes directly from the matching playbook rule — copy it, do not invent your own.
- Never fabricate a source_quote, clause_ref, page_number, or reasoning — if you did not find supporting text verbatim in the contract, source_quote, clause_ref, and page_number must all be null.
- Return ONLY raw JSON. No prose, no markdown fences, no commentary before or after.", messages: [ { role: "user", content: "Contract text:

" + $json.text + "

Playbook rules (JSON — extract exactly these fields, no others):

" + JSON.stringify($json.playbook_rules, null, 2) } ] }) }}

parameters.toolDescription: Fetches the contract playbook rules from the database based on contract type and stores them in shared memory. ALWAYS call this tool FIRST. Pass contract_type and intent.

options.systemMessage:
You are the Contract Playbook Agent. Your only job is to retrieve the correct 
playbook rules for the given contract type from the database and write a clear 
structured summary of those rules into shared memory.

YOUR PROCESS:
1. Use the fetch_playbook tool to query the contract_playbook table, filtered 
   by the provided contract_type.
2. Write a structured summary to memory in this format:

--- PLAYBOOK RULES FOR [CONTRACT_TYPE] ---
Intent: [intent]
Rules retrieved: [count]

- Rule Name: [key_term_name]
  Label: [key_term_label]
  Description: [key_term_description]
  Risk Weight: [risk_weight]

--- END PLAYBOOK RULES ---

3. Respond with: "Playbook loaded for [contract_type]. [N] rules stored in memory."

RULES:
- Do not extract terms. Do not analyze risk.
- If no rules found, write: "No playbook rules found for [contract_type]."

parameters.toolDescription: Fetches all playbook rules from the contract_playbook table filtered by contract_type. Returns key_term_name, key_term_label, key_term_description, risk_weight for each row.

conditions.keyValue: ={{ $fromAI('contract_type', 'The contract type to fetch playbook rules for', 'string') }}

parameters.content:
# Contract Analyzer — v4

## v4 additions (self-consistency voting + reasoning)
- key_term_extraction_agent's single agent-tool call was replaced with a direct-API loop: Prepare N Extraction Requests fans out to 3 items -> Extract Key Terms (Run N) calls the Anthropic Messages API directly (temperature 0.7, bypassing the LangChain agent-tool pattern entirely) -> Aggregate Self-Consistency Votes takes the 3 independent JSON outputs and, per playbook field, takes the majority value as the answer with the agreement fraction (e.g. "3/3", "2/3") as a real statistical confidence score, instead of the model self-rating its own confidence (not calibrated to anything) or a coarse binary Verified/Needs Review.
- Why not just have the Orchestrator call key_term_extraction_agent 3 times via prompt instruction: LangChain agents don't reliably self-loop a tool call a fixed N times from prompt text alone — the workflow itself (Prepare N Extraction Requests) guarantees exactly N calls, deterministically, not the LLM's own judgment.
- Orchestrator Agent's job shrank to STEP 1+2 only (intent + contract-type detection, then calling contract_playbook_agent) — its final output is now {contract_type, playbook_rules} as structured JSON, not the full extraction result.
- key_term_extraction_agent's output gained a `reasoning` field (1-3 sentences citing what the source text says) alongside the existing source_quote/clause_ref.
- GATE 2 ("Parse Result") gained a second, independent trigger: a term with NO majority at all across the 3 runs (every run disagreed) is flagged for human review regardless of risk_weight — "the model can't agree with itself" is its own reason for distrust, on top of the original high-risk-and-unverified trigger.
- Cost/latency tradeoff, stated plainly: this is 3x the API calls and 3x the latency of a single extraction call, on a pipeline that already ran ~30-60s per document. Deliberate choice (N=3, not N=5) to keep that tradeoff bounded — see README for the full reasoning.

## v3 additions (failure modes + human-in-the-loop)
- GATE 1 — "Sanity Check Extraction": deterministic check on extracted text (length + alphanumeric ratio) BEFORE any LLM call. Catches corrupted/scanned/encrypted PDFs at the earliest possible point instead of letting garbage text propagate through the agent pipeline.
- GATE 2 — "Parse Result" now computes needs_human_review: true only when a term is BOTH high risk_weight (4-5) AND has no source_quote. Escalates on uncertainty conditioned on stakes, not on risk alone (too broad) or missing-citation alone (too broad the other way). Deliberately NOT a third LLM classifier agent — an LLM deciding whether to trust an LLM is circular; this rule is auditable and uses data already computed.
- Every node that calls an external system now has explicit error handling: retryOnFail with a delayed retry (not exponential backoff — n8n's built-in retry is fixed-delay; true backoff would need a custom Code-based loop, noted as a gap) on Orchestrator Agent, both sub-agents, fetch_playbook, and both Supabase writes. Extract from File and Orchestrator Agent's error branches are now actually WIRED to a response instead of vanishing into continueErrorOutput with nothing connected (that was a real bug in v2 — errors were being silently swallowed).

## v3.1 fix — Task Runner hang
Parse Result originally used $('Webhook').item.json.body to grab file_name/intent for the audit log. On this self-hosted instance (n8n 2.21.7), a cross-node $('NodeName') lookup made from INSIDE Code-node JavaScript (executed in a separate Task Runner sandbox process) hung indefinitely — reproducibly, every run, isolated via single-node "Execute step" testing with pinned data. The same kind of lookup works fine as a parameter EXPRESSION on other node types (see Orchestrator Agent's own prompt, which does {{ $('Webhook').item.json.body.intent }} successfully) — expressions are evaluated by the main n8n process, not shipped out to the Task Runner over its (apparently broken) broker connection. Fix: removed file_name/intent from Parse Result entirely, since neither was actually used downstream by the frontend anyway — the fields existed only for a nice-to-have Supabase audit column. If you want them back, add a Set/Edit Fields node (parameter-expression based, not Code-node JS) between Orchestrator Agent and Parse Result instead of looking them up inside the Code node.

## v2 changes (still true)
- Session key is now per-execution ($execution.id) instead of a hardcoded "test_session" — fixes cross-request memory bleed between concurrent users.
- LLM swapped from OpenAI gpt-4o-mini to Claude (Anthropic Chat Model), currently Haiku 4.5 — cheap tier, sufficient for this scoped task. Tiered routing (stronger model reserved for whatever Gate 2 flags) is a verbal talking point, not built, to avoid adding LLM-on-LLM complexity.
- Added input validation (file present, type, size, intent) before processing.
- Results are written to Supabase `extractions` for an audit trail and observability.
- key_term_extraction_agent returns a verbatim source_quote per term (or null) — powers the citation click-through. No retrieval/vector DB — full text is already in context.

## Before running
1. Reconnect the Anthropic, Supabase (regular + tool) credentials — placeholders won't work.
2. The Supabase credential MUST use the service role/secret key, not the anon/publishable key — RLS is on with no policies.
3. Supabase project URL is already set to https://deezsambjmjmdqwodqhs.supabase.co
4. Replace the webhook's allowedOrigins with your real Vercel domain once deployed.
5. Run the updated supabase/schema.sql (adds needs_human_review, review_reason, and self_consistency_runs columns to extractions) — if you already ran an earlier version, just run the new ALTER TABLE lines at the bottom.
6. Extract Key Terms (Run N) is a plain HTTP Request node, not a LangChain node — it needs its OWN Anthropic credential selected (Authentication -> Predefined Credential Type -> Anthropic API) after import; it doesn't share the Anthropic Chat Model node's connection automatically.
